judgement.summary:
The production code of step 5 is in order and I re-measured every load-bearing claim myself on a throw-away copy under the session scratchpad (the real tree is byte-identical to how I found it: same `git status`, same md5s). The sanctioned suite on the real tree gives 3 failed / 387 passed / 13 deselected — the three known API-key/config environment failures named in SCOPE.md, nothing else. All five rulings of the first review are honoured in the code and each one is pinned by a test that really discriminates: `set(True)` -> `set(False)` at semantic_interpretation.py:1259 fails test_the_prefilter_decides_changed_below_the_threshold_and_defers_above_it; the old "set the flag, then always report" shape fails test_an_embedding_failure_skips_the_prefilter_for_the_rest_of_the_run[0.01]; `{str(exc) or type(exc).__name__}` -> `{exc}` at :1270 fails test_a_slow_embedding_call_is_cut_at_the_prefilter_timeout; dropping `or task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED` at :882 fails the new unrequested-answer test and nothing else. The plan edits match the shipped lines word for word (§5.4 Failures at plan:347-353, §15.5 at plan:1146-1171), §12 #5's approved text is untouched, and §15.8 stays correct. Nothing hacky went in: the diff between working_tree.diff and working_tree_v2.diff contains exactly the four fixes and the two hand-edited plan paragraphs.

What stops me short of "commit it" is the new test file, and only the test file. Four defects, all verified, all minor, all confined to archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py:

(1) The reset half of fix 1 is pinned by nothing. `assert not SE._embed_tracing_gated.get(), "and reset after it"` (test:528) runs in the test function's own context, while the flag was set inside a gate task that `asyncio.run` + `TaskGroup.create_task` gave a COPY of that context (PEP 567), so the read returns the module default False no matter what. I removed the `finally: _embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)` at semantic_interpretation.py:1272-1273 and the module still gave 32 passed. The package documented this exact trap 100 lines away, in the comment above test_complete_vector_store.py:314-317. A test that asserts a tautology while telling the reader it checks the reset should not be committed; I wrote and measured a 13-line replacement that passes on the shipped code and fails without the `finally`.

(2) `_run_under` (test:828-849) is a hand copy of `_Run.go`'s setup that has already drifted — it dropped the judge-shape assertions and the 20 s `wait_for`, which makes SCOPE.md's "Every run ... is bounded by a 20 s wait_for" untrue. I prototyped the two-line split that removes all 22 duplicated lines: 32 passed.

(3) `_caplog_at` (test:609-624) hand-rolls a logging handler that pytest's `caplog` fixture already provides and that test_deepseek_driver.py and test_layered_db.py in this same suite already use. I substituted `caplog` at all four call sites: 32 passed, and the substituted tests still fail under the `{exc}` mutation, so it is a faithful drop-in.

(4) In the new unrequested-answer test, `_counter() == c0` (test:417) cannot discriminate: with no `verdicts` the scripted judge defaults to "same", which never mints. Under the `_NOT_ENROLLED` mutation I probed all seven conditions of that test — six detect it, `counter` does not. Passing `verdicts={"T.d": False}` makes all seven detect it (measured both ways).

One correction to the challengers, because I ruled on the corrected version: tests-F2's headline consequence is half wrong. The mutant really does hang (I reproduced it: exit 124, empty log), but I then ran the same mutant through my split, i.e. with the 20 s `wait_for` in place — it hung just the same. A `wait_for` cannot bound a task that swallows its own cancellation, so the bound is not the remedy; the remedy is not to have a second copy of the harness at all.

Apply the four edits, re-run the module (32 -> 33 tests) and re-check that the new reset test fails with the `finally` removed, then commit. A further adversarial round is not warranted: none of the four touches production code, and I have measured each fix.

rulings.title: The tracing gate's "and reset after it" assertion is vacuous; the `finally` reset is pinned by nothing
rulings.rationale: Confirmed by my own mutation, not by trusting the finding. I removed `finally: _embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)` (semantic_interpretation.py:1272-1273) on a scratchpad copy and ran the module: 32 passed, nothing failed. So test_semantic_change_gate.py:528 (`assert not SE._embed_tracing_gated.get(), "and reset after it"`) cannot fail: the token is set inside a gate task that `asyncio.run` and `TaskGroup.create_task` each gave a COPY of the caller's context (PEP 567), so the read in the test function returns the ContextVar's module default False (semantic_embedding.py:38-39) either way. The SET half IS pinned — `set(True)` -> `set(False)` at :1259 fails test_the_prefilter_decides_changed_below_the_threshold_and_defers_above_it at line 526 (I measured one failing test, not the two the finding claims; immaterial). This is not a hypothetical or a style point: the same package wrote the lesson down in the comment at archive/tests/test_complete_vector_store.py:314-317 and pins its own gate correctly in test_gate_reset_in_same_task_context, and the new file does the very thing that comment forbids. The shipped code is correct on every path, so this is a defect in the test alone — but a test that asserts a tautology while telling the reader it checks the reset is worse than no assertion, and the first review's ruling machinery-F2 required set AND reset. NOTE: tests-tests-F1 is the same defect found independently; one edit closes both.
rulings.fix:
Delete the vacuous line 528, and pin the reset from inside a context where the set actually happened. I wrote and measured this (passes on the shipped code, fails with the `finally` removed, on both the success and the exception path):

    def test_the_prefilter_resets_the_tracing_gate_on_both_paths(cache):
        """The reset assertions MUST run in the task that awaited `_prefilter`:
        `asyncio.run` and every `create_task` copy the context (PEP 567), so a
        read after the run returns the default whatever the `finally` does."""
        async def go(provider):
            task = InterpretationTask(None, "/tmp/T.thy", "T", THY_KEY, [_entry("a", DG["a"])],
                                      emb_store=_FakeStore(provider), run_state=RunState())
            await SI._prefilter(task, task.entries[0], "the a", "new a")
            assert SE._embed_tracing_gated.get() is False
        asyncio.run(go(_FakeProvider()))
        asyncio.run(go(_FakeProvider(sims={"new a": ConnectionError("down")})))

(The judge-subclass variant the finding proposes also works; either is fine.) Keep the docstring's cross-reference to test_complete_vector_store.py::test_gate_reset_in_same_task_context so the two reset tests read as one lesson, and add "the `finally` reset removed" to SCOPE.md's mutation list.

rulings.title: The tracing-gate RESET is pinned by nothing (same defect as fixes-fix-T1)
rulings.rationale: Same defect as fixes-fix-T1, found independently and with the same evidence; I verified it once (removing the `finally` at semantic_interpretation.py:1272-1273 leaves the module at 32 passed) and the ruling is recorded there. Its proposed remedy — a direct `await SI._prefilter(...)` inside an `async def`, asserted on the success path and on a raising provider — is the one I prototyped and measured, so this entry's fix text is the one to follow. Apply ONE edit for both entries, not two.
rulings.fix: See fixes-fix-T1: delete test_semantic_change_gate.py:528 and add the direct `_prefilter` test that asserts `SE._embed_tracing_gated.get() is False` immediately after the await, once with a normal `_FakeProvider` and once with one whose `embed` raises.

rulings.title: `_run_under` is a hand copy of `_Run.go` that has already drifted (dropped judge-shape assertions and the 20 s bound)
rulings.rationale: The duplication is real and verified by reading: test_semantic_change_gate.py:828-849 restates, line for line, `_Run.go`'s setup at :229-256 (write T.thy, clear the driver override, delenv INTERPRETATION_DRIVER, build `_FakeProvider`, build `RunState` and monkeypatch `current_run_state`, build `_Connection`, define `make`, monkeypatch `make_interpretation_driver`), and the copy has already lost two things: the judge-shape assertions inside `make` (`cli_tools is False`, `system_prompt is _JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, one tool named "verdict", one entry) and the `asyncio.wait_for(..., 20)` that every other run carries — so SCOPE.md:116's "Every run ... is bounded by a 20 s `wait_for`" is untrue of exactly one run. That is the project's "never copy-paste-and-modify, refactor instead" rule with a demonstrated cost. BUT I reject the finding's headline consequence, having measured it: the mutant (`except asyncio.CancelledError: continue` before `except ReachLimitError:` in `_run_agent`) does hang the suite (timeout 40, exit 124, empty pytest log) — and it hangs identically WITH the 20 s bound in place. I applied the proposed split on the copy so the cancellation run went through `wait_for(..., 20)` and re-ran the same mutant: still exit 124. `wait_for` cannot bound a task that swallows its own cancellation, so "with the 20 s bound the same regression would have failed in 20 s" is false. The finding survives on reuse and drift, not on the hang.
rulings.fix: Split `_Run.go` at its last statement instead of copying it: keep everything through `self._mp.setattr(SI, "make_interpretation_driver", make)` in one method that RETURNS `asyncio.wait_for(SI.interpret_file(...), 20)`, and let `go` be `self.result = asyncio.run(<that>)` plus the post-run invariant. The cancellation test then reads `runner = asyncio.ensure_future(run.<that method>([_answer_batch()], entries, hold=hold))` and `_run_under` is deleted — 22 duplicated lines gone, the judge-shape assertions restored for this run too, and SCOPE.md:116 becomes true as written. I prototyped exactly this on the copy: 32 passed. Do not claim in SCOPE.md or a comment that the bound protects against a cancellation regression — measured, it does not.

rulings.title: `_caplog_at` reinvents pytest's `caplog`, which this suite already uses in two other modules
rulings.rationale: Verified as a defect of the "Always Reuse Code -- Never Reinvent the Wheel" rule, not as a style remark. test_semantic_change_gate.py:609-624 defines a 13-line context-manager class that attaches an ad-hoc `logging.Handler` to the `semantic_interpretation` logger; pytest ships this as `caplog`, and the same suite already uses it in the same `with ... at_level(...)` shape at test_deepseek_driver.py:126, :137, :245, :262 and test_layered_db.py:686. I did the substitution myself on the copy — `caplog` added to the four test signatures, `with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger=SI.__name__): records = caplog.records` at :562, :645, :662, :685 — and got 32 passed, so every message-content assertion survives; I then re-ran the `{str(exc) or type(exc).__name__}` -> `{exc}` mutation against the substituted file and test_a_slow_embedding_call_is_cut_at_the_prefilter_timeout still failed, so the substituted tests keep their discriminating power. The private helper buys nothing measurable and costs 13 lines plus an inconsistency with its neighbours.
rulings.fix: Delete `_caplog_at` (test_semantic_change_gate.py:609-624); take `caplog` as a fixture in the four tests that used it and write `with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger=SI.__name__): records = caplog.records`, matching test_deepseek_driver.py and test_layered_db.py. If there turns out to be a concrete reason the fixture does not fit, say what it is in the commit message rather than keeping the copy silently — I could not find one.

rulings.title: "counter untouched" is inert in the new unrequested-answer test: the scripted judge's default verdict never mints
rulings.rationale: Verified by my own probe. `run.go` is called at test_semantic_change_gate.py:412 with no `verdicts`, so `_ScriptedJudge.run_turn` falls back to `self._verdicts.get(self._name, True)` (:198) = "same" = UNCHANGED, which by §3 keeps the stored version and mints nothing. I replaced the assertion block at :413-417 with a non-fatal probe of all seven conditions and ran it under the mutation that removes `or task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED` from semantic_interpretation.py:882: `[('reply', False), ('interps', False), ('state', False), ('raw', False), ('counter', True), ('judged', False), ('judge_cost', False)]` — every condition detects the regression except `_counter() == c0`. Adding `verdicts={"T.d": False}` to the same call and re-running the probe gives `('counter', False)` too, i.e. all seven then detect it, and on the shipped code all seven hold. The plan names three assertions for this deliverable (§15.10: "record byte-identical, no judge driver constructed, counter untouched") and the docstring at :396-403 offers the counter as attribution evidence; as written the third one carries no weight against the regression the test exists for. Small, but it is a test claiming a check it does not make — the same family as the reset assertion above, and the fix is one argument.
rulings.fix: Change test_semantic_change_gate.py:412 to `res = run.go([act], entries, verdicts={"T.d": False})` and add a short trailing comment saying why a verdict is scripted for an entity that must never be judged (it is inert on the shipped code, and turns the CHANGED verdict on under any regression that lets the unrequested answer through, so the counter assertion and the docstring's "counter bump" become real). Measured: passes on the shipped code, and under the `_NOT_ENROLLED` mutation all seven conditions of the test now discriminate.

rulings.title: PROPOSAL: an `embed_tracing_gated()` context manager beside the ContextVar, replacing the two hand-written token/`finally` pairs
rulings.rationale: The facts are right and I checked them: the same four-line idiom (`token = _embed_tracing_gated.set(...)` / `try:` / `finally: _embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)`) now exists at semantic_interpretation.py:1259 + :1272-1273 and at semantics.py:2655 + :2704-2705, the ContextVar and its policy comment live at semantic_embedding.py:30-39, and the private name is imported by two other modules (semantics.py:28, semantic_interpretation.py:38). A context manager would make the reset impossible to forget, which is the project's own "a shape that makes an invariant impossible to violate beats one that asks people to remember it" rule, and finding fixes-fix-T1 shows the reset is exactly the half nothing was watching. Against it: the first review deliberately prescribed the raw pair and weighed a broader alternative before choosing the local one; the saving is about six lines over two call sites, which is not "markedly simpler"; semantics.py:2499 would still read the private ContextVar directly, so the private import does not go away; and semantics.py is outside step 5's files, which under this project's rules needs the user's explicit approval. So it is genuinely a call for the user, and the challenger was right not to smuggle it in. Not blocking: the shipped code is correct on every path I probed.

for_the_user: Optional, not blocking the commit: should the `_embed_tracing_gated` set/reset be wrapped in a small `embed_tracing_gated()` context manager exported beside the ContextVar in semantic_embedding.py, so the reset cannot be forgotten? It would remove the two hand-written token/`finally` pairs (semantic_interpretation.py:1259+1272-1273 and semantics.py:2655+2704-2705) at a cost of about six lines saved and one new helper. It needs your approval because it edits semantics.py, which is outside step 5, and because the first review deliberately prescribed the raw pair. Saying no costs nothing: the reset gets pinned by the new test either way.

findings.title: The tracing gate's "and reset after it" assertion is vacuous: dropping the `finally` reset leaves the whole module green, and the package already documented this exact trap
findings.claim: Fix 1 (machinery-F2) has two halves: set `_embed_tracing_gated` before the `try` and reset it in a `finally`. The new test pins only the first half. `assert not SE._embed_tracing_gated.get(), "and reset after it"` is evaluated in the test function's own context, while the set happened inside the task `asyncio.run` created — a PEP 567 context COPY — so the assertion reads the module default `False` whether or not the reset exists. It cannot fail. The `finally` at :1272-1273 is therefore shipped with no test at all, and the test carries a claim it does not check. This is not a hypothetical style point: the package already hit this exact trap once and wrote the lesson down in `archive/tests/test_complete_vector_store.py:315-320`, whose test is named `test_gate_reset_in_same_task_context` and whose comment reads "The reset assertions MUST run inside the same task context that awaited complete_vector_store: asyncio.run executes the coroutine in a COPY of the caller's context (PEP 567), so asserting after asyncio.run returns reads the default value whether or not the finally-reset exists." The step-5 test does the very thing that comment forbids.
findings.evidence: Measured on a throw-away rsync copy under the session scratchpad (the real tree was never modified; `git status` on the real tree still shows only the step-5 edits, and no test pointed at ~/.cache). (1) Mutation "remove the `finally: _embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)`" (semantic_interpretation.py:1272-1273): `python -m pytest archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py -q` → 32 passed, i.e. NOTHING fails, including line 528's assertion. Every other component of the four applied fixes does fail a test when mutated, which I re-measured on the same copy: `set(True)`→`set(False)` fails test_the_prefilter_decides_... and test_a_slow_embedding_call_... (2 failed); the old "set the flag, then always report" shape fails test_an_embedding_failure_..._[0.01] (1 failed); `{str(exc) or type(exc).__name__}`→`{exc}` fails test_a_slow_embedding_call_... (1 failed); dropping `or task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED` (:882) fails the new test_an_answer_for_an_entity_this_run_did_not_ask_for_is_refused. So the reset is the one unpinned piece. (2) A replacement assertion that DOES discriminate — recording the flag from inside the gate task, after `_prefilter` returned and while `_judge` runs in that same task — was written and run on the copy: it gives `[False]` on the shipped code (33 passed) and fails with `At index 0 diff: True != False` on the no-`finally` mutant. Whole-suite baseline on the copy: 386 passed / 3 pre-existing env failures (+1 more only because I had deleted Tools/ to keep the copy small, so SCOPE's 387/3 is confirmed). Also verified by reading and by probe, so the finding is only about the test, not the code: the token is set immediately before the `try` with nothing in between, the `finally` runs on the success, exception, timeout and cancellation paths (`except Exception` does not swallow `CancelledError`; an external cancel inside `asyncio.timeout` stays a `CancelledError`, probed on 3.12), and a probe that cancels the run while the gate is parked in the embed call leaves `prefilter_disabled` False, judges nothing and writes nothing.
findings.fix:
Replace line 528's vacuous assertion with one made from inside the gate task. The judge session runs in that same task right after `_prefilter` returns, and `_Run.go` already takes `judge_cls`, so a three-line subclass suffices (measured: passes shipped, fails with the `finally` removed):

    class _FlagRecordingJudge(_ScriptedJudge):
        seen: list[bool] = []
        async def run_turn(self, prompt: str) -> None:
            _FlagRecordingJudge.seen.append(SE._embed_tracing_gated.get())
            await super().run_turn(prompt)

Use it in the prefilter test (or a small test of its own) with `run.go([...], entries, verdicts={...}, judge_cls=_FlagRecordingJudge)` and `assert _FlagRecordingJudge.seen == [False], "reset before the judge runs"`. Name `test_gate_reset_in_same_task_context` in the docstring so the two reset tests are visibly one lesson, and add "the `finally` reset removed" to SCOPE.md's mutation list.

findings.title: PROPOSAL: the token/`finally` dance for the tracing gate now exists twice; a context manager beside the ContextVar would make the reset impossible to forget
findings.location: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:1259 and :1272-1273; Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:2655 and :2704-2705; the ContextVar at semantic_embedding.py:38-39
findings.claim: After fix 1 there are two production copies of the same four-line shape (`token = _embed_tracing_gated.set(...)` / `try:` / `finally: _embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)`), plus two more in `test_complete_vector_store.py:246-251` and `:281-285`. The project rule is that a shape which makes an invariant impossible to violate beats one that asks people to remember it, and finding fix-T1 shows what is being remembered here: the reset is exactly the half nothing pins. A `@contextlib.contextmanager` exported beside the ContextVar — `with embed_tracing_gated():` in `_prefilter`, `with embed_tracing_gated(not verbose):` in `complete_vector_store` — removes both copies of the bookkeeping and gives the gate one documented entry point instead of a private name imported across three modules. I am raising this as a proposal, not a bug: the shipped code is correct on every path I probed, and the judge's ruling prescribed the raw set/reset pair, so this is a call for the user rather than something to smuggle in.
findings.evidence: Read on disk: semantic_interpretation.py:1259/1272-1273 and semantics.py:2655/2704-2705 are byte-for-byte the same idiom around different bodies; semantic_embedding.py:38-39 defines the ContextVar with the comment explaining why it must be a ContextVar, i.e. the module already owns the policy but not the entry point. The private name `_embed_tracing_gated` is now imported in two other modules (semantics.py:28, semantic_interpretation.py:38) and in the tests. No behaviour would change: I verified the two production sites are plain dynamic-extent gates with no other use of `token`.

findings.title: The tracing-gate RESET is pinned by nothing: `assert not SE._embed_tracing_gated.get()` reads the test's own context and can never fail — the trap this package already documented
findings.claim: Ruling machinery-F2 required the gate to be set before the `try` AND reset in a `finally`. The set half is pinned (`provider.tracing_gated == [True, True]`, verified discriminating). The reset half is pinned by nothing. Line 528 asserts `not SE._embed_tracing_gated.get()` AFTER `run.go(...)` has returned, i.e. in the test function's own context; `_prefilter` sets the ContextVar inside a gate task spawned by `TaskGroup.create_task` under `asyncio.run`, and every one of those layers runs on a COPY of the caller's context (PEP 567), so the outer read returns the module default `False` whether or not the `finally` exists. The assertion is a tautology dressed as a check. This is not a subtle discovery in this repo: `archive/tests/test_complete_vector_store.py:314-317` carries a comment written for exactly this trap -- "The reset assertions MUST run inside the same task context that awaited complete_vector_store: asyncio.run executes the coroutine in a COPY of the caller's context (PEP 567), so asserting after asyncio.run returns reads the default value whether or not the finally-reset exists" -- and its `test_gate_reset_in_same_task_context` does it correctly. The new file reproduces the mistake that comment exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: Measured on a throw-away rsync copy under the session scratchpad (PYTHONPATH-shadowed; the real tree was never modified, every test drives the `cache` fixture's tmp_path SEMANTIC_DB_DIR). Baseline on the copy: 4 failed / 386 passed / 13 deselected (the 3 known env failures plus one test_layered_db case that is a copy artifact -- the real tree gives the SCOPE's 3 failed / 387 passed, which I also ran). Mutation: comment out `finally:` / `_embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)` at semantic_interpretation.py:1272-1273. Result: 4 failed / 386 passed / 13 deselected -- byte-identical failure list, and `test_semantic_change_gate.py` alone stays 32 passed. Nothing fails. For contrast the SET mutation (`set(True)` -> `set(False)` at :1259) does fail exactly one test (`test_the_prefilter_decides_changed_below_the_threshold_and_defers_above_it`), which is how a real pin behaves.
findings.fix: Delete the vacuous line 528 and pin the reset the way `test_complete_vector_store.py::test_gate_reset_in_same_task_context` already does: assert INSIDE the awaiting context. Concretely, add a small test that awaits `SI._prefilter(task, e, baseline, fresh)` directly inside an `async def go()` and asserts `SE._embed_tracing_gated.get() is False` immediately after the await, once on the success path and once with a `_FakeProvider` whose `embed` raises (the exception path is the one the `finally` exists for) -- the task and `_FakeStore`/`_FakeProvider` are already available in the module, and `_judge_task`'s `InterpretationTask(None, ...)` shows how to build a bare task.

findings.title: `_run_under` is a hand-copy of `_Run.go`'s body that dropped the 20 s `wait_for`, so a cancellation regression hangs the suite forever instead of failing
findings.claim: `_run_under` restates, line for line, the setup half of `_Run.go` -- write T.thy, clear `interpretation_driver_override`, delenv INTERPRETATION_DRIVER, build the `_FakeProvider`, build the `RunState` and monkeypatch `current_run_state`, build the `_Connection`, define `make`, monkeypatch `make_interpretation_driver` -- and then calls `interpret_file` itself. Two things fell off in the copy: the judge-shape assertions inside `make` (`cli_tools is False`, `system_prompt is _JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, one tool named "verdict", one entry) and, load-bearingly, the `asyncio.wait_for(..., 20)` bound that every other run in the file carries. SCOPE.md states "Every run ... is bounded by a 20 s `wait_for`" and plan §15.10 states the discipline in as many words ("under `asyncio.wait_for` so a regression fails instead of hanging"); the cancellation test is the one run where neither holds. It is also the run where it matters most: the test's whole shape is `runner.cancel()` then `await runner`, and the scripted judge is parked on an `asyncio.Event` that is never set, so a regression that stops the cancellation from propagating leaves `await runner` blocked with nothing to time it out. This is duplication with a measured consequence, which is what the project's "Always Reuse Code -- Never Reinvent the Wheel" rule is about.
findings.evidence: Demonstrated on the scratchpad copy. Mutation (a plausible broadening of a retry arm) inserted before `except ReachLimitError:` in `_run_agent` at semantic_interpretation.py:1520: `except asyncio.CancelledError:` / `continue`. Command `timeout 30 python -m pytest archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py -q -k cancellation` exited 124 with an EMPTY log -- pytest never produced a line and had to be killed; the run hangs indefinitely. (For contrast, a mutation that merely swallows the cancellation in `_judge` -- `except Exception` -> `except BaseException` at :1265 -- fails cleanly in 1.4 s, so the hazard is specific to regressions that keep the run alive, which is precisely the class a cancellation test guards.) With the 20 s bound the same regression would have failed in 20 s.
findings.fix: Split `_Run.go` at its last line instead of copying it: keep everything through `self._mp.setattr(SI, "make_interpretation_driver", make)` in one method that returns the un-awaited `SI.interpret_file(...)` coroutine, and let `go` be `self.result = asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(<that coroutine>, 20))` plus the post-run invariant. The cancellation test then does `runner = asyncio.ensure_future(asyncio.wait_for(run.<that method>([_answer_batch()], entries, hold=hold), 20))` and `_run_under` disappears -- 22 duplicated lines gone, the bound restored, and the judge-shape assertions apply to this run too.

findings.title: `_caplog_at` reinvents pytest's built-in `caplog`, which this very suite already uses
findings.claim: The new file defines a 13-line context-manager class that adds an ad-hoc `logging.Handler` to the `semantic_interpretation` logger and collects records. pytest ships exactly this as the `caplog` fixture, and this suite already uses it in the same `with caplog.at_level(...)` shape in `archive/tests/test_deepseek_driver.py:126` (and :137, :245, :262) and `archive/tests/test_layered_db.py:686`. Writing a private replacement for a facility the neighbouring test modules already use is the "never reinvent the wheel" rule's exact case, and it costs the file 13 lines plus the reader's question "why not caplog here?".
findings.evidence: Verified as a drop-in on the scratchpad copy: I replaced all four `with _caplog_at(logging.WARNING) as records:` sites with `with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger=SI.__name__):` / `records = caplog.records` and added `caplog` to the four test signatures, leaving `_caplog_at` unused. Result: `python -m pytest archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py -q` -> 32 passed. Every message-content assertion (the single "did not respond" line, the per-failure host-log count, the "judge gave no verdict" absence, the `startswith("T:")` absence, "no embedding store") holds unchanged.
findings.fix: Delete `_caplog_at` and take `caplog` as a fixture in the four tests, `with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, logger=SI.__name__): records = caplog.records`, matching test_deepseek_driver.py and test_layered_db.py.

findings.title: In the new unrequested-answer test, "counter untouched" is the one assertion that cannot discriminate — the scripted judge's default verdict never mints
findings.claim: `test_an_answer_for_an_entity_this_run_did_not_ask_for_is_refused` was added to pay §15.10's named deliverable, and its docstring says "any judge session or counter bump could only be the unrequested answer's" -- inviting the reader to treat the counter check as load-bearing. It is not. `run.go` is called with no `verdicts`, so `_ScriptedJudge.run_turn` falls back to `self._verdicts.get(self._name, True)` = "same" (:198), which is UNCHANGED, which never mints. With the `_NOT_ENROLLED` guard removed, T.d's smuggled answer therefore runs a full gate (prefilter at the default 0.95, then a judge session) and writes "unrequested" over the cached record WITHOUT moving the counter. The plan's three named assertions are "record byte-identical, no judge driver constructed, counter untouched"; two of the three bite, the third is inert as written, and one extra argument makes it bite too.
findings.evidence: Measured on the scratchpad copy. Mutation: `semantic_interpretation.py:882` `if idx is None or task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED:` -> `if idx is None:`. The test fails (it is the SOLE guard: 1 failed / 31 passed in the module), stopping at the first assertion. I then replaced the assertion block with a non-fatal probe of all seven conditions and re-ran under the same mutation: `PROBE [('reply', False), ('interps', False), ('state', False), ('raw', False), ('counter', True), ('judged', False), ('judge_cost', False)]` -- every condition detects the mutation except `_counter() == c0`. Changing the single call to `run.go([act], entries, verdicts={"T.d": False})` and re-running the same probe gives `('counter', False)` along with all the others, i.e. all seven then discriminate. Both files restored afterwards; the module is back to 32 passed.
findings.fix: Pass `verdicts={"T.d": False}` to `run.go` at :412 -- on the shipped code no judge ever runs for T.d, so the argument is inert, and under any regression that lets the unrequested answer through it turns the CHANGED verdict on, making the counter assertion (and the plan's own wording about a "counter bump") real.

verified_ok: Fix 1, the tracing gate, is correct on every path. `token = _embed_tracing_gated.set(True)` sits immediately before the `try` with nothing between them (semantic_interpretation.py:1259-1260), and the `finally` at :1272-1273 runs on the success path, on the `except Exception` path (whose `return None` still runs the finally), on the `asyncio.timeout` path (TimeoutError is an Exception in 3.11+, so it is caught) and on cancellation (`except Exception` does not swallow BaseException). Probed on Python 3.12: an external `task.cancel()` inside `async with asyncio.timeout(60)` comes out as CancelledError, not TimeoutError, so a cancelled gate cannot be mistaken for a failed embed; and an end-to-end probe on the copy (cancel the run while the gate is parked in a 5 s embed) ends with `prefilter_disabled` False, `run.judged == []`, the record byte-identical and no §12 #5 line.

The gate is scoped to the gate task's own context and cannot leak sideways: `start_gate` creates each gate with `task_group.create_task` (:655-670), which copies the context (PEP 567), so a concurrent `_auto_embed` or a concurrent gate cannot see another gate's token — which is exactly the reason semantic_embedding.py:36-37 gives for the flag being a ContextVar rather than a global.

It gates exactly the embed machinery's tracing and nothing the user must see. `Embedding_Provider._log` (semantic_embedding.py:433-439) is the only gated emitter on the `embed()` path, and it writes solely to `conn.tracing`; `_warn` (:441-451) has no gate check, so the retry ladder's HTTP-error detail lines at :366 still reach the user's warning channel; `_report` (semantic_interpretation.py:960-982) never consults the flag, so the §12 #5 line awaited INSIDE the still-gated `except` block is unaffected. The other tracing calls in that module (:696-767, :1443) belong to `_embed_batch` / `query`, which `_prefilter` never reaches — it calls `emb_provider.embed`, whose backend is `self._embed`.

The gate does not cost the diagnosis of a connection-layer failure, which was my main worry about suppressing :361. Probed: because the ladder's `await asyncio.sleep(2 ** attempt)` runs INSIDE its `except Exception as e:` handler, the timeout's CancelledError is raised with that handler's exception as `__context__`, and `asyncio.timeout` chains `TimeoutError from CancelledError`. So `_prefilter`'s `_log.warning(..., exc_info=True)` at :1264-1265 prints the whole chain — the underlying `ConnectionRefusedError`/httpx error included — into the host log. Verified with a standalone 3.12 probe reproducing the ladder's shape.

Fix 2, `claim_prefilter_disable` (:358-364), makes "once per run" true for all three populations. Gates already parked inside the failing `embed`: each reaches the handler, but only the first claim returns True — measured by the parametrised test at delay 0.01 (2 embed calls, 2 host-log failure lines, exactly 1 §12 #5 line), and the old "set the flag, then report" shape fails that parametrisation. Gates entering after the flip: the guard at :1255 returns None before the `try`, so they neither embed nor report. The startup-check case with the flag preset: the same guard suppresses the line, and `interpret_file` (:1737-1741) additionally leaves `emb_store` None, so the guard's first disjunct fires too — pinned by test_an_unconfigured_service_means_no_store_and_the_judge_alone. The read-and-flip is one synchronous step: `first, self.prefilter_disabled = not self.prefilter_disabled, True` evaluates the RHS tuple, then assigns, with no await and no yield point in between; a method rather than an inline pair, so it cannot be split by a later editor.

Fix 3, the `<error>` slot `str(exc) or type(exc).__name__` (:1269-1270). I looked for an exception whose `str` is non-empty but useless and found none that is actually reachable. Within the 60 s bound almost nothing but `TimeoutError` can escape `embed`: the ten-step ladder (semantic_embedding.py:352-372) catches every `Exception` from the backend and sleeps 1+2+4+8+16+32 s, so HTTP-status, connection and DNS errors are all still being retried when the timeout cuts in — which also means the message-bearing HTTP cases keep reaching the user through the ungated `_warn` at :366 and never through this slot. The message-bearing case that does exist (`ConnectionError("embedding service down")` in the test) is byte-identical to the old rendering, so the exact-line assertion still discriminates. As a by-product this rules out an API-key leak through the slot: no httpx exception carrying a `?key=` URL can escape the ladder inside 60 s.

Fix 4's test does pin what it claims: removing `or task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED` from the answer tool (:882) fails test_an_answer_for_an_entity_this_run_did_not_ask_for_is_refused and nothing else (measured, 1 failed / 31 passed).

The plan edits describe the code exactly. §5.4 Failures (plan:347-353) now says "once per run: the caller that flips the flag is the one that reports — `RunState.claim_prefilter_disable()`, §15.5 — so ... are one operation even for the gates already inside the failing call", which is what :1266-1270 does. §15.5 (plan:1150-1171) now describes the tracing gate ("set before the `try` and reset in a `finally`"), the claim-then-report handler and the `str(exc) or type(exc).__name__` slot; each sentence matches the shipped lines. §12 #5's "once per run" is restored rather than contradicted, and its `<error>` slot is unaffected by the class-name fallback.

No other plan sentence went stale. §15.8's "Run-scoped state" (plan:1403-1423) still describes `RunState`'s field and the startup check SETTING `prefilter_disabled` directly — which remains correct and, with the new method, still suppresses §12 #5 (a direct set makes every later claim return False), so §5.6 (plan:483) needs no edit either. §15.10's step-5 bullet already named the deliverables the fixes touched ("unrequested-answer rejection and its mirror", "the prefilter timeout") and both are now covered; §15.11's "After step 5" bullet and §12 #5's approved wording are unchanged by the fixes. The only plan/code gaps I found in this area are the two pre-existing pseudocode liberties in §15.5 (argument order `_prefilter(task, rec.baseline_interpretation, text, e)` vs the shipped `(task, e, baseline, fresh)`, and `verdict = await _judge(...)` vs the shipped bool), which are older than these fixes and were passed by the first review.

No import cycle from the new `from .semantic_embedding import _embed_tracing_gated` (semantic_interpretation.py:38): semantic_embedding imports nothing from semantics or semantic_interpretation (its imports are lines 1-24), and the pattern matches the established one at semantics.py:28.

gate-F1's test, the [0.01] leg: it really does put a and b inside ONE failing embed call. `monkeypatch.setattr(SI.AgentTask, "batch_size", 2)` takes effect (probe: batch 2, 2 turns), so the first turn answers a and b together and `on_answer` starts both gates in the same tick; with `delay=0.01` gate a is suspended inside `_FakeProvider.embed` when gate b passes the `prefilter_disabled` guard and enters it too. Probe of the fresh texts of the recorded calls: delay=0.0 -> ['new a']; delay=0.01 -> ['new a', 'new b']. c is answered only after the flag flipped (its action polls `run.run_state.prefilter_disabled`, and the bound is 200 x 1 ms so a regression fails rather than hangs), and `len(provider.calls) == 2` pins that c made no embed call.

gate-F1's test discriminates against the OLD shape. Mutation: replace `if task.run_state.claim_prefilter_disable(): await _report(...)` at semantic_interpretation.py:1266-1270 with `task.run_state.prefilter_disabled = True` followed by an unconditional `await _report(...)`. Result: `test_an_embedding_failure_skips_the_prefilter_for_the_rest_of_the_run[0.01]` FAILS (two "The embedding service did not respond" lines), `[0.0]` passes -- exactly the split the parametrisation was added for. The companion assertion `sum("prefilter: the embedding call failed" in ...) == len(provider.calls)` also correctly pins "log the traceback unconditionally" (1 log at delay 0, 2 at delay 0.01).

machinery-F2's test sees the flag INSIDE the embed call: `_FakeProvider.embed` appends `SE._embed_tracing_gated.get()` as its second statement (test:130, :136), before any await, and `test_the_prefilter_decides_changed_below_the_threshold_and_defers_above_it:526` asserts `[True, True]`. Mutation `set(True)` -> `set(False)` at semantic_interpretation.py:1259 fails exactly that test. (Only the SET is pinned -- see tests-F1 for the reset.)

agreement-F4's test pins the class-name line: `test_a_slow_embedding_call_is_cut_at_the_prefilter_timeout` asserts `lines == ["The embedding service did not respond: TimeoutError"]`. Mutation `{str(exc) or type(exc).__name__}` -> `{exc}` at semantic_interpretation.py:1270 fails exactly that test with the dangling-colon line "The embedding service did not respond:".

agreement-F1's deliverable really guards the clause: with `task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED` removed from semantic_interpretation.py:882 the new test fails and it is the only test in the whole suite that does (module: 1 failed / 31 passed; suite: failure list otherwise byte-identical to baseline). Six of its seven conditions discriminate (see tests-F4 for the seventh).

The zero-norm guard in `_cosine` is pinned: deleting `if not (nu > 0.0 and nv > 0.0): return None` (semantic_interpretation.py:1235-1236) fails `test_the_prefilter_is_scale_free_and_a_zero_vector_is_not_computable` (ZeroDivisionError -- the norms are Python floats, so 0.0/0.0 raises rather than producing NaN), and the shipped path the test claims (zero vector -> not computable -> the judge decides) is what the passing assertions check.

`_embed_tracing_gated` covers every tracing line the prefilter's `embed` can emit: `Embedding_Provider.embed`'s two lines (semantic_embedding.py:465, :467), `_embed_cached`'s cache lines (:337, :340), the per-chunk line (:348) and the retry-ladder failure line (:361) all route through `self._log`, which returns early on the flag (:434). `_warn` stays ungated as documented at :35, and `Semantic_Vector_Store.embed_records`'s tracing (semantics.py:2499) is not on this path at all (the prefilter calls `emb_provider.embed` directly). The whole-DB use in `complete_vector_store` (semantics.py:2655, reset at :2704) is a different task's context and cannot cross with a gate's.

The plan edits match the code: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §5.4 Failures (lines 347-353) and §15.5 (lines 1146-1170) now describe `claim_prefilter_disable()`, the `_embed_tracing_gated` set/reset, and the `str(exc) or type(exc).__name__` slot exactly as semantic_interpretation.py:358-364 and :1246-1273 implement them; §12 #5's approved text is unchanged.

Suite state on the real tree, with the sanctioned command: 3 failed / 387 passed / 13 deselected -- the two `test_config_resolution` cases and `test_embedding_provider_refactor::test_fireworks_qwen`, the known API-key/config environment failures, matching SCOPE.md.
